allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Gunslinger Jonah Hex is appointed by President Ulysses Grant to track down terrorist Quentin Turnbull, a former Confederate officer determined on unleashing hell on earth. Jonah not only secures freedom by accepting this task, he also gets revenge on the man who slew his wife and child.

facts.title: Jonah Hex

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Can Jonah Hex halt Turnbull's devastating plan before the rogue officer unleashes his ultimate catastrophe?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Commissioned by President Ulysses Grant, scarred gunslinger Jonah Hex hunts down Quentin Turnbull, a Confederate officer set on unleashing hell on earth and the man who slaughtered Hex's family.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Fast, gritty, and suspenseful supernatural action built for a focused solo watch or casual group night.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: At a lean 81 minutes, Jimmy Hayward's fast-moving fantasy thriller fuses grit and apocalyptic stakes into a propulsive hunt fueled by pure vengeance.

claudeAdvisory.claimSpan: a Confederate officer set on unleashing hell on earth and the man who slaughtered Hex's family
issueSummaries: description's appositive structure ('Quentin Turnbull, a Confederate officer set on unleashing hell on earth and the man who slaughtered Hex's family') identifies Turnbull as the man who killed Hex's family. The overview says only that Jonah 'gets revenge on the man who slew his wife and child' and never says this is Turnbull. The copy therefore asserts an identity link the packet leaves open. It also touches the spoiler boundary on culprit information.

description drops 'former' from 'former Confederate officer' and adds 'scarred', which appears only in facts.keywords ('facial scar') and not in the overview or allowedSourceMaterial.keywords. Both are small unsupported factual attribute changes.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Most of the copy is grounded or is tolerated figurative language and genre shorthand under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1 ('devastating plan', 'ultimate catastrophe', 'apocalyptic stakes', 'propulsive hunt'). The substantive issue is the description's phrasing, which identifies Turnbull as the killer of Hex's family. That falsely specifies an identity and relationship link that the packet leaves unstated, and it sits close to the excluded 'culprit information' category. It does not contradict the source, reveal a later event or ending, or invent a new character, so it is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would keep the two facts separate, for example 'hunts down Quentin Turnbull, a former Confederate officer set on unleashing hell on earth, and gets a shot at revenge for his family's death'.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: the overview gives two separate facts, that Turnbull is a former Confederate officer determined on unleashing hell on earth, and that Jonah gets revenge on 'the man who slew his wife and child'. It never states these are the same person. The copy merges them. 'Slaughtered... family' intensifies 'slew his wife and child' and is tolerated wording on its own.

description: Jonah Hex as a gunslinger, appointment by President Ulysses Grant ('commissioned' paraphrases 'appointed'), the hunt for Quentin Turnbull, and the plan to unleash hell on earth all restate the overview. The order of the two Turnbull facts is what creates the merger. 'Set on' paraphrases 'determined on'. 'Hunts down' paraphrases 'track down'.

curiosityHook: 'halt Turnbull's devastating plan' and 'rogue officer' restate the plan to unleash hell on earth and the Confederate officer background. 'Before... unleashes his ultimate catastrophe' is figurative urgency in the class of the tolerated 'before mom returns'. The interrogative asserts no outcome.

whyWatch and vibeSummary: 'fantasy thriller' and 'supernatural action' are consistent with genres Fantasy/Thriller/Western and the 'hell on earth' framing, so I treat them as tolerated shorthand. 'Jimmy Hayward' and '81 minutes' match director and runtimeMinutes. 'Apocalyptic stakes' and 'propulsive hunt fueled by pure vengeance' are thematic shorthand. Vengeance is stated in the overview, though the copy does not need it to be tied to Turnbull.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Fast' and 'fast-moving' match pace=fast. 'Suspenseful' matches moods. 'Gritty' is tonal shorthand. 'Focused solo watch or casual group night' matches attentionDemand=engaged and situations=[friends, alone]. Keyword-only material (tomahawk, comic book) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. The overview places the revenge clause immediately after the Turnbull sentence, so a reader would probably infer that Turnbull is the killer, and an adjudicator could treat the copy as a harmless reading of that ordering and approve. I flag it because the closed-world rule treats packet-absent identity links as ungrounded, and because the copy states the link outright where the packet leaves it implicit. 'Scarred' (from facts.keywords only) and 'Confederate officer' without 'former' are minor and could be approved alone. If Sophia treats facts.keywords as valid grounding, 'scarred' would fall away.

geminiAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: All visible editorial copy strictly complies with A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The starting premise, central characters, historical backdrop, and vengeance motive in the description and curiosityHook faithfully adhere to the authorized overview and verified keywords without importing external comic lore (such as DC Comics history or unstated mystical powers) or violating setup-only spoiler boundaries. Phrasing such as 'slaughtered Hex's family' for 'slew his wife and child' and 'apocalyptic stakes' for 'unleashing hell on earth' operates as legitimate, low-risk paraphrase and metaphorical framing, while experiential descriptors in whyWatch and vibeSummary map cleanly to verified baseline facts and authorized semantic tags.
